issues.description: NamespaceSealed is a stub that lies — returns false always while ACLs and listing already trust it
issues.detail: core.go adds (*Core).NamespaceSealed that always returns false with a TODO. Meanwhile ListAllNamespaces, root-token paths, and the new ErrNamespaceSealed handling are being wired to it as if it works. That's not a stub, that's a security regression with a comment on it. Ship the SealManager in the same patch or return an error/panic until it exists; do not let production code paths call a function that silently claims 'nothing is sealed.'

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES — ACL semantics change, response_util refactor, ctx plumbing, and stubs jammed into one diff
issues.detail: This is at least three patches: (1) ACL root becomes namespace-scoped with HasParent ancestry check, (2) sdk response_util rewritten from if-chain to switch, (3) wholesale s/context.Background()/namespace.RootContext(t.Context())/ across dozens of tests plus stubs. Each deserves independent review and bisectability. The ACL change alone is a security-critical semantic shift and should land alone with focused tests.

issues.description: ACL fast-path silently returns deny on namespace.FromContext error instead of failing loud
issues.detail: AllowOperation now does ns, err := namespace.FromContext(ctx); if err != nil { return ret }. Empty ACLResults means denied with no log, no signal. Previously the root fast-path didn't need ns at all. Now a missing namespace in context silently denies every root operation. At minimum log; better, distinguish 'no namespace' from 'denied' — this is exactly the kind of silent failure that bites at 3am.

issues.description: HasParent ancestry check for root tokens needs an explicit security test, not just a happy-path child-ns test
issues.detail: The semantic change is: a root token issued in ns A now grants root in any descendant of A. testACLRoot only checks self-ns allow and root-context deny. Where's the test for sibling namespace denial? Cousin? Deeply nested descendant allow? Root-of-root behavior when a.root is RootNamespace? This is the ACL — the table you do not get wrong. Cover the matrix exhaustively or this lands as a latent privilege escalation waiting for the right ns tree.

issues.description: errwrap.Contains on ErrNamespaceSealed.Error() string-matches 'namespace is sealed' anywhere in any error
issues.detail: Reusing the same errwrap.Contains(err, ...Error()) pattern means any error message containing the substring 'namespace is sealed' — including ones constructed by handlers, plugins, or audit logs — will be coerced to 503. The existing ErrSealed pattern has the same flaw; you're propagating it. Prefer errors.Is on the sentinel. While you're refactoring this function into a switch anyway, fix the actual bug.

issues.description: NSTokenLength = TokenLen + "\".\"[1] + nsID is cute; just write TokenLen + 1 + NSIDLen
issues.detail: Indexing into a string literal to get the byte value of '.' as a length contribution is the kind of cleverness that wastes the next maintainer's two minutes. If it's a constant length, write the constant. If '.' is the separator, name a const Separator = "." and use len(Separator). BAD-TASTE — not wrong, just gratuitously opaque for a length arithmetic.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The ACL change is the real patch here and it is a security-critical semantic shift — root tokens now grant root across descendant namespaces via HasParent — wrapped in a diff that also rewrites response_util, retrofits ctx plumbing across a dozen test files, and ships a NamespaceSealed stub that returns false while callers already depend on it. THREE-PATCHES at minimum. Split the ACL change out, write the full ancestry permission matrix in tests (sibling/cousin/deep-descendant), do not land a stub that lies about seal state in production code paths, and stop string-matching error messages — use errors.Is on the sentinel. Refuse until the SealManager exists or NamespaceSealed errors loudly until then.
